laws.rule: From 1 November 2026 Carinthia charges a stay levy (Aufenthaltsabgabe) of EUR 3.60 per person per night plus an infrastructure and mobility contribution of EUR 0.90 per night (about A$5.72 and A$1.43 at EUR 0.6293 per A$1, RBA 30 Oct 2026), under section 4(1) of the Kärntner Aufenthaltsabgabegesetz (K-AAG). On a campsite pitch that the campsite operator does not supply, the stay levy is EUR 3.10 (about A$4.93). Young people up to the end of the calendar year they turn 16 are exempt (section 3(1) item 3). The law replaces the earlier Ortstaxe system. Operators who find breaches face fines of up to EUR 1,000 (section 11(3)).
laws.heading: K-AAG, paragraphs 3, 4 and 11

laws.rule: In open countryside (freie Landschaft) in Carinthia it is banned to pitch a tent or park a caravan or motorhome outside approved campsites and outside garden-type areas next to houses (section 15(1) of the Kärntner Naturschutzgesetz 2002). Exceptions include alpine bivouacking, a weather shelter for fishing, temporary non-commercial tent camps, short-term caravan parking on road-parking areas, and building-site set-ups (section 15(2)). The on-the-spot fine for breaking it is EUR 50 (about A$79 at EUR 0.6293 per A$1, RBA 30 Oct 2026), item 10 of the schedule to the Kärntner Naturschutz-Organstrafverfügungsverordnung.
laws.heading: K-NSG 2002, section 15; K-NOV Anlage 1 item 10 (RIS Landesrecht)

laws.rule: Carinthia: without a supervising person, children may not be in public places, restaurants, Buschenschank wine taverns, club rooms or at public events from 23:00 to 05:00, and young people up to the end of their 16th year not from 01:00 to 05:00. This does not apply if there is a good reason (section 8(1) and (2) of the Kärntner Jugendschutzgesetz). Who counts as a child is set in the law's definitions, which were not read.
laws.heading: K-JSG, section 8

laws.rule: Carinthia: up to the end of the 16th year, buying, having and drinking alcohol is banned. From 16, drinks with distilled alcohol (above 0.5% alcohol) are banned, and any other alcohol is allowed only below 0.5 g/l blood alcohol or 0.25 mg/l breath. Children and young people are also barred from buying, having, using and passing on tobacco products, water pipes, e-shishas and e-cigarettes (section 12(1) to (3) of the K-JSG).
laws.heading: K-JSG, section 12

items.text: Carinthia's youth-protection law (K-JSG, section 12) does not limit the alcohol rules to public places only. Under 16: no alcohol. From 16 to 18: no spirits of more than 0.5% alcohol by volume, and other alcohol may be consumed only up to a blood-alcohol limit of 0.5 g/l (0.5 Promille) or 0.25 mg/l in breath; the police may require a breath test. A person who is married or serving in the Bundesheer or Zivildienst is treated as 18. Supply of alcohol in the course of a trade is dealt with under the Gewerbeordnung, not this section. Fines: adults generally up to EUR 3,630 (about A$5,768); supply for profit, EUR 2,000 to EUR 20,000 (about A$3,178 to A$31,781); a young person up to EUR 500 (about A$795), or EUR 1,000 (about A$1,589) for a second repeat.

psychoactive-substances.notes: These are Land youth-protection rules, not a general adult drinking age of 18 for beer or wine. They apply to visitors under 18 in this Land. Federal narcotics law is not restated here. AUD at the RBA rate of 30 October 2026, A$1 = EUR 0.6293. Official RIS consolidated text (Geltende Fassung) read directly on 11 November 2026.
